title: 苔
author: 袁枚
intro: Twenty characters about moss: it grows where the sun never reaches, its “flowers” are as small as grains of rice — and still it blooms as proudly as the peony. A tiny poem that became famous all over China in 2018, when village children sang it on TV.
analysis: 这首诗写的是最不起眼的青苔。第一句写它生长的地方：太阳照不到的阴暗角落。可是第二句一转：就算在这样的地方，春天的生机也照样自己来了——“青春”在古诗里指春天、草木青绿的生命力，不是今天说的“年轻时光”；“恰”字有一种“偏偏、照样”的意思。后两句最有名：苔藓的“花”像米粒那么小，却也学着牡丹的样子开放。牡丹又大又艳，被叫作“花中之王”，苔花和它一比，小得几乎看不见，但它不自卑，也要尽情地开一次。诗人借写苔表达一个道理：再平凡、再弱小的生命，也有自己的价值，也有开花的权利。这种借物说理的写法和《石灰吟》《竹石》一样，叫“托物言志”。2018年，央视节目《经典咏流传》里，支教老师梁俊带着贵州山区的孩子唱了这首诗，感动了很多人，这首几百年来不太出名的小诗从此家喻户晓。
analysisEn:
This poem is about one of the most overlooked things in nature: moss. The first line tells us where it lives — in shady corners the sunlight never reaches. Then the second line turns: even there, the life of spring arrives all by itself. In old poetry 青春 means spring and the fresh green energy of growing things, not “youth” as it does today. The little word 恰 adds a sense of “all the same, just as it should”.

The last two lines are the famous ones. The moss’s “flowers” are as small as grains of rice, yet they also try to bloom like the peony. (Botanically, moss has no flowers — the tiny heads are spore capsules — but to the poet they are flowers.) The peony is big and showy, called the “king of flowers”; next to it the moss flower is almost invisible. But it does not feel small. It blooms anyway, with everything it has.

Through the moss, the poet says something about people: even the most ordinary, humble life has its own worth and its own right to flower. Writing about a thing to express an idea like this is called 托物言志, the same method as in Song of Lime and Bamboo and Rock.

For centuries this was a little-known poem. Then in 2018, on the CCTV programme Classics Sung Today (经典咏流传), the volunteer teacher Liang Jun sang it with children from a poor mountain village in Guizhou, and it moved the whole country.
background: Yuan Mei (1716–1798) was a Qing poet and essayist who left official life in his thirties and spent decades in his Garden of Contentment (随园) in Nanjing. He believed poetry should come from real, personal feeling, and he often wrote about small, everyday things — like the cowherd boy in What I Saw, or this moss.
pronunciation: 恰 qià；苔 tái（青苔、苔藓的“苔”；“舌苔”读 tāi）；处 chù（地方）；牡丹 mǔ dān。
version: 采用通行本。袁枚原作《苔》共两首，这是第一首，也是最常被选读、传唱的一首；第二首文字不同，网站不收。

lines.lit: The place the bright sun does not reach —
lines.en: Where sunlight never finds its way,

lines.lit: green spring still comes there by itself.
lines.en: spring still arrives, all on its own.

lines.lit: Moss flowers, as small as rice grains,
lines.en: The moss puts out flowers as tiny as rice,

lines.lit: also learn to open like the peony.
lines.en: yet they bloom like the peony all the same.

words.note: 现代汉语说“太阳”“白天”；成语“白日做梦”还在用。
现代汉语“到处”“好处”“住处”。

words.en: green spring — the fresh life of spring
words.note: 古义指春天、草木青绿的生机；现代汉语指年轻的时光，如“青春期”。
现代汉语“恰好”“恰恰”“恰当”。

words.en: by itself; of its own accord
words.note: 现代汉语“自己”“自然”“自动”。
书面语，口语说“像”；现代汉语“如同”“如此”。
这里是“模仿”的意思，现代汉语也说“学他说话”“学猫叫”。
现代汉语仍用；牡丹被称为“花中之王”，洛阳牡丹最有名。

imagery.name: 苔
imagery.zh: 青苔长在没有阳光的角落，又小又不起眼，却照样生长、开花，象征平凡弱小的生命也有自己的价值和尊严。
imagery.en: Moss grows in sunless corners, tiny and unnoticed, yet it lives and “flowers” anyway — ordinary, humble lives have their own worth and dignity.

imagery.name: 牡丹
imagery.zh: 牡丹是“花中之王”，又大又艳；米粒大的苔花也要学它开放，大小对比之下，更显出小生命不自卑、要尽情绽放的勇气。
imagery.en: The peony is the showy “king of flowers”; set beside it, the rice-sized moss flower that still dares to bloom shows the courage of small lives.
